title: Stacked townhouse rezonings and new city auditor
subtitle: Trussler Road proposal deferred; Turner Avenue infill, KPMG audit contract and a private street name also considered.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee dealt with two rezoning applications for stacked townhouses. For 9-27 Turner Avenue, it recommended approval of a 30-unit development, which will also be the first development application subject to the city's rental replacement by-law. For 60 Trussler Road, a 63-unit proposal, the committee recommended referring the matter to the November 18 Council meeting so the applicant and staff can discuss fewer and smaller units and options for a visual barrier {{vote:m4}}.

The committee also recommended awarding the city's audit services contract to KPMG LLP for a three-year term with options to renew, and acknowledged a proposed private street name, Bridlewood Crescent, for a development on Hidden Valley Road.

These are recommendations, so Council must still adopt or change them. For residents near Trussler Road, the deferral gives more time to raise concerns about privacy, drainage, traffic and housing mix. The Turner Avenue approval adds homes in an established neighbourhood, with sidewalks to be built or funded through the development process.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended referring the rezoning to the November 18, 2024 Council meeting so the applicant and staff can discuss fewer and smaller units and options for a visual barrier.
The committee recommended approving the zoning change to allow stacked townhouses at 9-27 Turner Avenue.

The committee recommended awarding the audit services contract to KPMG LLP at an estimated total of $665,909 including HST for three years, with options for two one-year renewals, and amending the Municipal Code to appoint KPMG LLP as auditor.
The committee acknowledged the developer's intent to name a private street Bridlewood Crescent at 980 and 1018 Hidden Valley Road and directed Legal Services to prepare the naming by-law.

debate: Delegates opposing the Trussler Road proposal raised concerns about drainage onto neighbouring lands, loss of privacy for backyards on Cora Drive, a lack of sustainability features, and rent control exemptions. One delegate felt the scale did not fit the neighbourhood.

Staff said the building was placed away from the low-rise homes. Staff said the applicant agreed to a taller visual barrier, and that engineering staff confirmed sanitary capacity and will require a stormwater management plan.

Several councillors questioned the lack of three-bedroom units. The applicant's planner said the stacked layout does not suit them. Staff said the city does not regulate bedroom counts and noted most existing homes in Kitchener already have three or more bedrooms.

The councillor who moved the deferral said a one-unit reduction did not answer neighbours' concerns. That councillor asked for fewer units, some three-bedroom units and a full visual barrier. Others suggested affordable units and asked the applicant to attend in person.

On Turner Avenue, councillors supported gentle intensification. Questions focused on sidewalks, which staff said would be built by the city or funded by the developer, and on how the rental replacement by-law protects current tenants.
